correctness.rationale: Enumerates every forbidden induced triple and every dual face in each of eight n. An exact augmented integral chain complex is verified to square to zero and reduced entirely via unimodular unit-pivot cancellations, leaving precisely one nonzero integral Betti degree; an independent unreduced mod-2 elimination reproduces it. Signed Hopf traces are evaluated exhaustively at all 264 rotations and reflections, with every trace independently matched by direct fixed faces of the original cut complex, avoiding an unverified Alexander-duality sign. Character averages are exact integers; rational quotient homology agrees with invariants by finite-group averaging after barycentric subdivision. No floating-point or incomplete enumeration.

originality.rationale: The original published integer Betti ranks (Chauhan–Shukla–Vinayak Table 2), the shellability threshold and the large-order complete dihedral character do not specify the 264 rotation/reflection traces at 13<=n<=20 or their quotient invariant dimensions. The complete 2024/2025 Table 2, 2026 primary power-cycle paper and two very relevant publicly available prior results were compared by mathematical implication; full published scope of the latter results is n>=21 or n>=27, respectively. The new calculation is an entire new equivariant invariant, not a rank recomputation; equivalence in unindexed work is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed publication may have computed equivalent small-order dihedral characters.
All computations and source comparisons are same-model; independent mathematical priority and verification are not established.

value.rationale: A complete, natural equivariant classification on the exact finite window in which the usual shellability theorem does not apply. The invariant quotient homology jumps to rank 4 only at n=16 and n=17 and vanishes for all six other orders, a structural distinction not inferable from the already-published nonequivariant ranks. At n20, the rank-four action splits into two different two-dimensional dihedral constituents. Useful boundary data for finite-group actions on graph cut complexes; not an arbitrary isolated integer.
